dimensions.note: Unchanged: token is sensitive in the global schema and comes from a vault expression; the fetch transport in repo_settings.ts masks the token wherever a response echoes it; Octokit receives it only as auth. writeRecord logs only data names, never a token.

Every method logs its outcome at info with structured placeholders. writeRecord warns once per repository, with {legacy} and {name} as properties, the first time it writes a portable name while the pre-2026.11.08.1 name holds data, and points at the README for the removal. Verified live: one warning on the first run, none on the second, none for a repository never listed.

The REST transport throws before any writeResource with method, path, status and GitHub's message; repoDelete treats 404 as absent. readOrNull swallows every error from readResource deliberately: the read-back only decides whether to print the notice, and a name Windows cannot store fails at the path rather than as not-found; the write itself still surfaces its own errors.

The three repo_settings methods and the check are tested with a strict fake caller and a mocked fetch. New: dataName rejects every character Windows refuses and a trailing dot, keeps the three specs distinct and never starts with upstream's repo- prefix; legacyDataName matches what the old safeName produced; writeRecord warns once and never twice, stays quiet without old data, without readResource and when the old name cannot be read; branches_list end to end writes branches-<repo>. 22 tests. Still open from upstream: the four Octokit methods (sync, ensureRepo, ensureRelease, openPr) have no injectable client.

Unchanged: ensureRepo, ensureRelease and openPr find existing state first; default_branch_ensure reports unchanged; repo_delete treats absent as a no-op. Kept from upstream: ensureRepo creates only and never converges an existing repository's settings. The name change is non-destructive: nothing deletes, renames or rewrites data under an old name; removal is the user's swamp data delete --prefix, documented with its dry run.
Unchanged: every page of repositories, releases and pulls through Octokit paginate; branches_list follows every page up to a cap and records truncated. No Retry-After handling.
No files, handles or cloud resources beyond what is recorded; every request carries the method's abort signal. The two read-backs in writeRecord run concurrently and hold nothing.
README and tests use acme, tool, example-org and forge.example.net; the issue links point at the public tracker and the Swamp Club lab. No real hosts or account identifiers.

Unchanged: every schema is a plain z.object; the info objects written are the schema types themselves, so schema-write conformance holds field for field (owner, repo, defaultBranch, branches, truncated, timestamp; owner, repo, defaultBranch, action, timestamp; owner, repo, action, timestamp).

All seven resource specs declare lifetime infinite and garbageCollection 10; the README says so in one place. An item left under an old name is never expired by GC, which is why the README gives the explicit delete.
Unchanged: releases and pull requests are create only, as upstream designed. Narrow by intent.
Unchanged: github-token-accepted (label live) runs before every method and proves the token and that it can see the owner.

Enumerated: repos; repo-<slug>; release-<slug>-<slug>; pull-<slug>-<slug>-<slug>; branches-<repo>; default-branch-<repo>; delete-<repo>. The three follow upstream's shape: spec word first, parts joined with -, the repository through the same slug helper, no owner since the owner is the model's. Each spec is written by one method; the first words differ from upstream's repo- so a repository named delete-x cannot collide with a delete receipt. No ':' anywhere (dataverket-org/swamp-extensions#1, swamp-club/swamp#3205); the repository is reduced to [A-Za-z0-9._-] with trailing dots trimmed. Verified live against swamp 20261106: the portability warning the old names drew is gone.

writeRecord reads back the latest record under the new and the old name through context.readResource, both tolerant of failure, only to decide whether to print the one-time notice; it uses nothing beyond the documented context API, never reads another behavior's data and never deletes. Old data is left in place; the README documents its removal with swamp data delete --prefix, dry run first, verified live.

Version 2026.11.08.1 with a no-op upgrades entry after the 2026.10.05.1 one; the global arguments are unchanged, so a definition is stamped and not transformed. The chain is chronological and tested to end at the model's version. Verified live: an instance created at 2026.10.27.1 reports typeVersion 2026.11.08.1 and staleness current after one run.
